about: BlackSwan curated watch list: new threat actors, AI attack tools and campaigns. Updated by BlackSwan's daily research agent and by hand. Each item: date (YYYY-MM-DD), level (2 caution, 3 danger, 4 critical), title, actor, summary, source (URL), iocs {ips, domains, userAgents}.

items.title: Thousands of exposed AI hacking servers now probing the internet
items.actor: Operators of ARTEX, AntiFox, PentestCode and PentAGI instances
items.summary: Shadowserver counts about 4,200 internet-facing AI attack-framework servers, with over 80 actively probing VPNs, web apps and developer tools such as Jenkins and hunting for .env secret files. Patch internet-facing systems, keep secrets out of web folders and rate-limit repeated probes.

items.title: 1Password breach: expect convincing phishing using real account details
items.summary: An attacker used a stolen employee GitHub account to copy 1Password source code and some customer account records (names of accounts, sign-in times, setup and recovery tokens). Vaults and passwords were not taken. Ignore emails asking for your password or Secret Key; open the official app instead of clicking links.

items.title: GT13 campaign breaks into Check Point firewall management servers
items.summary: Attackers took over about 24 Check Point Security Management servers at 22 organisations in 17 countries, stealing firewall settings and passwords and switching off protections. Organisations using Check Point should patch CVE-2026-16232 now and check management servers for unknown admin activity.

items.title: Black Friday phishing surge impersonates major shops
items.summary: Fake Black Friday deals, delivery notices and refund messages pretending to be Amazon, Apple, eBay, Netflix, PayPal and others have risen sharply, especially in the US and Canada. Do not click links in deal or delivery messages; open the shop’s official app or website yourself.

items.title: Unit 42: autonomous AI agents run full intrusions after web-shell break-ins
items.summary: In over 10 campaigns, attackers planted web shells on vulnerable web apps, then let AI agents explore, steal passwords, gain admin rights and spread to cloud and partner systems, running hundreds of commands an hour. Patch public web apps, enforce MFA and sign-in limits, and watch for sudden bursts of commands.

items.title: CERT-In: AI-assisted attacks trigger unauthorised payments in India
items.summary: Attackers using AI tools break into banks, fintech and payment providers, change payee or approval records, then send money to mule accounts through normal payment systems. Check payee changes carefully, report unexpected transfers to your bank immediately, and businesses should review payment approvals.

items.title: Russian Cold Relic uses MFA fatigue, then poses as victims to breach partners
items.summary: Russian spies tired out a Google Workspace admin with repeated MFA prompts, copied the whole company's data, then emailed a partner organisation pretending to be a staff member. Never approve sign-in prompts you did not start, and check unusual requests from known contacts by phone.

items.title: ARTEX AI attack framework in widespread criminal and state use
items.actor: ARTEX users (Storm-0940, VAPOR PANDA, Storm-3358, Crafty Falcon)
items.summary: Open-source AI agent framework used to scan targets, guess passwords at thousands of attempts a minute and abuse secrets leaked on GitHub, reaching cloud data within minutes. Public copies on Docker Hub (tomicdd/artex, congdonglinux/artex) were backdoored.

items.title: China-linked group uses Cairn AI framework for autonomous espionage
items.summary: Attackers drove the open-source Cairn AI pentest framework against at least 19 organisations, including semiconductor suppliers, US defence and policy groups and human-rights organisations, getting in at 10. Patch internet-facing software, reduce exposed services and protect accounts with strong MFA.

items.title: AntiFox attack tool built on ARTEX code
items.summary: Attacks reported using AntiFox, a tool derived from ARTEX. Expect the same behaviour: bursts of automated requests, password spraying and leaked-secret abuse.

items.title: Storm-3358 targets financial firms with ARTEX
items.summary: Financially motivated group using ARTEX against financial-sector organisations, exploiting unrestricted file uploads and server-side request flaws, then installing open-source remote-access tools.

items.title: AI agents hunt GitHub for leaked secrets
items.summary: Agents search public repositories for company names plus words like secret and cloud or AI provider names, then sign in with what they find. Rotate any key ever committed, even if the commit was deleted.
